## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`preview` has to be fixed before merge because its "outside home" check does not catch path traversal. `Path.is_relative_to` compares paths as text without resolving them, so a relative path containing `..` can read any file the process can access. The only added outside-path test passes an absolute path, so it does not exercise this case.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `preview(home, "../../etc/passwd")` reads and returns `/etc/passwd` when it should raise `ValueError("outside home")`. The candidate `home/../../etc/passwd` is never resolved, and `PurePath.is_relative_to` only checks whether the text starts with `home`, so the check passes. A symlink inside `home` that points outside it also gets through. To fix this, resolve both sides first (`root = Path(home).resolve()`, `candidate = (root / relative).resolve()`, then `candidate.is_relative_to(root)`). Then add a test with a `"../outside.txt"` relative path, because the current case at tests/test_paths.py:20 (an absolute `tmp_path / "outside.txt"`) only covers the absolute-path branch. — Any caller that passes a user-supplied relative path can read the first 200 characters of arbitrary files outside the selected home directory, which is the exact case the guard exists to stop.

- The new tests check the 200-character truncation with a 500-character file (tests/test_paths.py:17-18), so a change to the preview length would be caught.
